hero.heading: Extend Crustates, safely.
hero.lead: Barnacle plugins are sandboxed WebAssembly components running in Wasmtime. Each one declares the capabilities it needs, and you approve them on install. A broken or malicious plugin can't reach anything you didn't grant.

dialog.title: Install ntfy alerts
dialog.note: No file system, no shell, no access to VMs or apps.

security.heading: Capabilities, not trust.
security.lead: Plugins only see the host through WIT interfaces. Anything not granted simply doesn't exist inside the sandbox.
rows: Create or change resources through the API

Approve or reject changes before they apply
Manage records for a DNS provider

Render a panel in the console

items.title: Signed
items.body: Packages are OCI artifacts signed with Sigstore. Unsigned plugins need an explicit admin override.

items.title: Fuel and memory limits
items.body: Each call gets a CPU budget and a memory cap, so a runaway plugin is stopped, not your host.

items.title: Audited
items.body: Every API call a plugin makes is in the audit log under its own identity.

build.heading: From zero to installed in four steps.
build.lead: Write plugins in Rust, Go, TypeScript or Python: anything that compiles to a WASI 0.2 component. The SDK and WIT interfaces are Apache-2.0.

steps.title: Scaffold
steps.body: Pick a template: event hook, DNS provider, alert channel, storage driver, policy or widget.

steps.title: Declare capabilities
steps.body: List what you need in barnacle.toml. Ask for as little as possible.

steps.title: Test locally
steps.body: crust barnacle dev runs it against a node with hot reload and a fake event stream.

steps.title: Publish
steps.body: Push the signed component to any OCI registry and submit it to the directory.

hood.heading: Wasmtime and the component model.
hood.lead: Plugins target WASI 0.2 today and move to 0.3 once runtimes settle. Interfaces are defined in WIT and versioned with the API, so plugins keep working across releases.
